detail.body:
## Overview

Draft-path fastpaths for DSV4.1-Flash serving on gfx950 (MI355X), all three on the DSpark draft prepare step that runs before every draft CUDA-graph replay: shared-output dedup across draft KV cache groups, a parallel pad-tail fix, and a KV-only context insert (dummy-Q removal). All three levers are conditional (kill switches) and engage on ROCm only — every other platform keeps the stock paths, unchanged and silent.

Part of the DSV4.1-Flash MI355X serving fastpath series — four **independent** single-commit PRs, each reviewable and mergeable separately, in any order. Siblings: #63179 (tiny-M quant fusion + lm_head guard), #63180 (fused shared experts), #63181 (fused draft sampling). The four series PRs all register kill switches in `vllm/envs.py` at the same anchor and therefore conflict textually with each other there; the resolution is to keep both sides. This branch is rebased onto current `main` (no textual conflicts; diff unchanged from the original submission).

## Claims

- **Shared-output dedup** (`dflash/speculator.py`): with multiple draft KV cache groups (the DSpark draft model's hybrid KV layout; 3 at the measured TP=4 shape), `prepare_dflash_inputs` runs once per group, but only the per-group outputs differ between calls — every other output is a pure function of the same inputs and is recomputed identically on each call. The dedup computes the shared outputs on the first call only (`SKIP_SHARED` constexpr in the Triton kernel) and skips them on calls 2..N: bit-exact by construction, since the skipped stores would rewrite identical values into the same shared buffers. Kill switch `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_DRAFT_PREPARE_DEDUP`; ROCm-gated.
- **Parallel pad-tail** (same file): the stock kernel pads `[q_pad_start, max_num_tokens)` of each draft group's query slot mapping serially from one CTA, on every per-group call. The fix skips the in-kernel tail (`PAD_TAIL=False`) and pads `[q_pad_start, HWM)` for all draft group rows in one parallel launch, `HWM = min(max_num_reqs * num_query_per_req, max_num_tokens)`; the draft replay only ever reads slot mappings up to `num_tokens_padded` (eager steps and uniform captured graphs alike), so the fix is bit-exact by construction for every read-visible cell. Kill switch `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_DFLASH_PREPARE_PAD_FIX`; ROCm-gated.
- **KV-only context insert** (`dspark.py`): `precompute_and_store_context_kv` used to allocate a zero dummy query and run the fused Q+KV ops with the full q_head_padded, discarding the quantized-Q output. It now calls the existing `fused_deepseek_v4_kv_rope_insert` (#56441) with zero query heads — the same call `nvidia/dspark.py` makes here — so the dummy-Q allocation, its zero-fill and the quantized dummy-Q write disappear on every cache dtype. Kill switch `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_DRAFT_CTXKV_DUMMYQ`.
- **−281 µs decode ITL (−5.0%) on the current base** (`main`@`717cf84342`) — official DSV4.1-Flash serving command at TP=4 on MI355X, complete separation on per-run medians (rebase re-check under Validation). First measured **−5.7% / −15.7%** (−323 / −985 µs, sampled / greedy) on the submission-base nightly ROCm-10 image with fully disjoint per-run ranges; re-checks across bases hold the win at −281 to −290 µs. TTFT flat within noise (draft-path only).

## Validation

**Benchmark (nightly ROCm-10 A/B)** — official serving command (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, DSpark k=5, `--monokernel`, MI355X), measured at TP=4 on the current nightly ROCm-10 image (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm`, digest `98beb734…`); the three mechanisms are TP-size agnostic (the draft KV group count varies with layout). Both arms run this PR's head; the OFF arm disables only this PR's three levers. Fresh server per arm, warmup + 1 sampled + 1 greedy client run (16 prompts, ISL 16 / OSL 2048, concurrency 1); lever engagement asserted from the server log before the client runs.

Per-run results — run1 (sampled) and t0 (greedy), one fresh server per arm:

| | run1 (sampled) | t0 (greedy) |
|---|---|---|
| mean ITL — ON (ms) | 5.298 | 5.274 |
| mean ITL — OFF (ms) | 5.621 | 6.259 |
| mean ITL — delta | −323 µs (−5.7%) | −985 µs (−15.7%) |
| mean TTFT — ON / OFF (ms) | 17.1 / 17.3 | 16.8 / 24.6 |
| spec-decode acceptance length — ON / OFF | 3.45 / 3.24 | 4.91 / 5.09 |

ITL ranges fully disjoint (ON max 5.298 below OFF min 5.621 by 323 µs). Sampled-run TTFT flat; the OFF greedy run is that arm's slow run on both ITL and TTFT (run-to-run scatter — the levers touch only the decode draft path, never prefill). Spec-decode acceptance parity (the three levers are bit-exact at op level).

**Rebase re-check** — the branch is rebased onto current `main` (`717cf84342`; diff unchanged) and re-verified with the same protocol (one fresh boot per arm, 2 sampled + 1 greedy run, census-asserted engagement on both arms): ON 5.330/5.282 vs OFF 5.611/5.617/5.577 ms (sampled / greedy) — median of per-run mean ITL ON 5.330 vs OFF 5.611 → −281 µs (−5.01%), complete separation on per-run medians (ON 5.289–5.328 below OFF 5.588–5.632); the first ON sampled run hit isolated ~30 ms server stalls (mean 6.217, median 5.318 — in line with the clean runs, same transient noted on the other PRs in this series). Matches the prior-base re-check (−290 µs on `c50aca1441`).

**Accuracy** — gsm8k, 5-shot, strict match, 1319 samples, one run per arm: ON 0.9257, OFF 0.9272. Both inside the 0.9196–0.9340 band observed across repeated draws of this build. The three levers are bit-exact at op level, so the on/off gap is the engine's run-to-run scatter (batch-composition-dependent decoding), not lever numerics; across the series the paired on/off deltas scatter on both sides of zero and every arm score lands inside the band.

**Tests** — all tests pass locally on MI355X (gfx950):

```
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py -q
10 passed
```

`test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py` runs on any GPU (the fastpath tests patch the platform gate): the pad-fix parametrization pins the bounded-write contract (`[q_pad_start, HWM)` padded with the stock PAD values, rows past HWM untouched — never read by any draft-path consumer) and the stock full-tail contract; the new two-draft-groups test runs the dedup at non-zero group ids (shared outputs bit-identical to the per-group recompute, the parallel pad touching only the draft group rows); the gate test pins the stock paths on non-ROCm platforms. The op-level `q_head_padded=0` contract is covered by the existing `test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py` (runs on MI355X DPX CI); the earlier standalone op-test file is deleted. The full pre-commit suite passes on the changed files (ruff, typos, mypy, check-torch-cuda-call, check-test-tethering, ...), and the commit is DCO-signed.

The benchmark and the tests above are measured on this PR's head, rebased onto current `main`; the rebase introduced no textual conflicts and the diff is unchanged from the original submission.

<details><summary>Reproduction</summary>

Server (ON arm) — official serving command, as measured at TP=4 (the fastpaths are not TP=4-specific):

```
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 --port 8123 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --moe-backend aiter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --block-size 128 --monokernel \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

OFF arm: identical, plus `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_DRAFT_PREPARE_DEDUP=1 VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_DFLASH_PREPARE_PAD_FIX=1 VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_DRAFT_CTXKV_DUMMYQ=1`.

Load (after a 4-prompt warmup; add `--temperature 0` for the greedy run):

```
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --port 8123 --backend openai --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 16 --random-output-len 2048 \
  --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 --ignore-eos \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 90,95,99 \
  --save-result
```

Accuracy (same engine config; `max_model_len 16384` and no `cpu_offload` are the only harness deviations):

```
python -c '
import lm_eval
lm_eval.simple_evaluate(
    model="vllm",
    model_args=dict(
        pretrained="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017",
        max_model_len=16384, tensor_parallel_size=4,
        tokenizer_mode="deepseek_v41", gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,
        block_size=128, moe_backend="aiter", monokernel=True,
        attention_config={"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4",
                          "indexer_sparse_logits": True},
        compilation_config={"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 6, 8]},
        speculative_config={"method": "dspark",
                            "num_speculative_tokens": 5,
                            "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic",
                            "rejection_sample_method": "block",
                            "enable_adaptive_verification": False}),
    tasks=["gsm8k"], num_fewshot=5, batch_size=8)'
```

</details>

## Details

Engagement lines are WARNINGs (the rust-frontend server logs carry no INFO records): the dedup engaged/DISABLED pair, the pad-fix engaged/DISABLED pair (scope=process, one per TP rank), and the ctxkv engaged line (the raw kill var's disabled side is silent — OFF is proven by the engaged line's absence). All of these fire on ROCm only; non-ROCm platforms log nothing and keep the stock paths (pinned by a test).

`q_head_padded=0` (KV-only insert) is covered at op level by `test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py`; `test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py` pins the prepare contracts described above.

Related: #58633 rewrites the same in-kernel pad tail with a different bound (full buffer vs this PR's `[q_pad_start, HWM)`); whichever lands second should rebase and re-measure.

This replaces the stock pad tails with one parallel launch. Stock: the prepare kernel pads `[q_pad_start, max_num_tokens)` of every draft group's query slot mapping serially from a single CTA, inside every per-group call. Here the in-kernel tail is skipped (`PAD_TAIL=False`) and all draft-group rows are padded in one parallel Triton launch bounded to `[q_pad_start, HWM)`, where `HWM = min(max_num_reqs * num_query_per_req, max_num_tokens)` bounds every read of the buffer (eager steps and captured-graph pads alike), so the bounded pad is bit-exact for every read-visible cell — the proof now sits inline at the launch. The launch is eager, in `propose()`, so no CUDA-graph capture constraints apply. 

By using HWM limit, the padding avoids redundant work.
